target: Ρώτησα έναν κύριο για τον δρόμο.
english: I asked a gentleman for directions.
tip: Asking for directions is ρωτάω για τον δρόμο (rótisa gia ton drómo = I asked about the way).

target: Αργήσαμε γιατί είχε πολλή κίνηση.
english: We were late because there was a lot of traffic.
tip: 'There was traffic' uses έχω: είχε κίνηση (eíche kínisi = there was traffic).

target: Πήγατε πουθενά το σαββατοκύριακο;
english: Did you go anywhere at the weekend?
tip: πουθενά (pouthená) flips by context: 'anywhere' in questions – Πήγατε πουθενά; (pígate pouthená) – but 'nowhere' with δεν (den).

target: Η συνάντηση άρχισε στις εννιά ακριβώς.
english: The meeting started at nine sharp.
tip: ακριβώς after a time = sharp: στις εννιά ακριβώς (stis enniá akrivós = at nine sharp).

target: Μίλησα με το αφεντικό για τον μισθό.
english: I talked to the boss about the salary.
tip: το αφεντικό (boss) is neuter, even for a man: μίλησα με το αφεντικό (me to afentikó).

target: Οργάνωσες εσύ τη συνάντηση;
english: Did you organize the meeting?
tip: Adding εσύ stresses WHO: Οργάνωσες εσύ; (orgánoses esý = was it YOU who organized it?)

target: Ο συνάδελφός μου άργησε πάλι σήμερα.
english: My colleague was late again today.
tip: μου pulls a second accent onto long words: ο συνάδελφός μου (o synádelfós mou = my colleague).

target: Τηλεφώνησα στην εταιρεία δύο φορές.
english: I called the company twice.
tip: You phone TO someone: τηλεφώνησα στην εταιρεία (tilefónisa stin etaireía = I called the company) – with nouns, τηλεφωνώ (tilefonó) takes σε (se).

target: Έγραψα δύο γράμματα το απόγευμα.
english: I wrote two letters in the afternoon.
tip: The έ- (e-) in έγραψα (égrapsa = I wrote) only carries stress. When stress moves, it drops: γράψαμε (grápsame = we wrote).

target: Η Σοφία έγινε γιατρός πέρσι.
english: Sofia became a doctor last year.
tip: No 'a' before jobs: έγινε γιατρός (égine giatrós = she became a doctor) – professions drop the article after becoming-verbs.

target: Μπόρεσες να τελειώσεις την αναφορά;
english: Were you able to finish the report?
tip: Μπόρεσες; (bóreses = did you manage?) – the past of μπορώ (boró) means a one-off success, 'managed to', not just general ability.

target: Έκλεισα το παράθυρο γιατί έκανε κρύο.
english: I closed the window because it was cold.
tip: Weather stays in the imperfect as background: έκανε κρύο (ékane krýo = it was cold).

target: Άνοιξες την πόρτα στη γάτα;
english: Did you open the door for the cat?
tip: Greek opens the door TO someone: άνοιξες την πόρτα στη γάτα; (ánoixes tin pórta sti gáta = did you open the door for the cat?) – σε (se), not για (gia).

target: Κοιμήθηκα νωρίς χθες το βράδυ.
english: I went to sleep early last night.
tip: κοιμήθηκα (koimíthika = I slept) looks passive but isn't – sleep, remember and fear only have passive-shaped forms, so their past ends in -θηκα (-thika).

target: Χθες γνώρισα τον αδερφό της Μαρίας.
english: Yesterday I met Maria's brother.
tip: γνώρισα (gnórisa) = met for the first time. Meeting up with someone you already know is είδα (ída = I saw) instead.

target: Γνώρισες τους γονείς του;
english: Have you met his parents?
tip: English 'have you met' is plain past in Greek: Γνώρισες; (gnórises) covers both 'did you meet' and 'have you met' – no perfect needed.

target: Ο Νίκος μου είπε ένα μυστικό.
english: Nikos told me a secret.
tip: Little words like μου sit right before the verb: μου είπε (mou eípe = he told me).

target: Σου έδωσα τα λεφτά προχθές.
english: I gave you the money the day before yesterday.
tip: 'To you' comes before the verb: σου έδωσα (sou édosa = to-you I-gave) – the little word lands in front.

target: Τα παιδιά γέλασαν με το αστείο του παππού.
english: The kids laughed at grandpa's joke.
tip: You laugh WITH something in Greek: γέλασαν με το αστείο (gélasan me = they laughed at).

target: Ο γιος μου έγινε δέκα χρονών χθες.
english: My son turned ten yesterday.
tip: Turning an age = γίνομαι + χρονών: έγινε δέκα χρονών (égine déka chronón = he turned ten).

target: Πήγαμε βόλτα στο πάρκο το απόγευμα.
english: We went for a walk in the park in the afternoon.
tip: πάω βόλτα = go for a stroll: πήγαμε βόλτα (pígame vólta = we went for a walk).

target: Μιλήσατε με τη δασκάλα για τον μικρό;
english: Did you talk to the teacher about the little one?
tip: ο μικρός / η μικρή = the kid, an affectionate everyday word: για τον μικρό (gia ton mikró).

target: Ο σκύλος έφαγε το φαγητό της γάτας.
english: The dog ate the cat's food.
tip: The of-form follows the thing owned – reverse of English: το φαγητό της γάτας (to fagitó tis gátas = the food of-the-cat = the cat's food).

target: Έμαθες τα νέα για τον Κώστα;
english: Did you hear the news about Kostas?
tip: μαθαίνω (mathaíno) is both learn and find out: Έμαθες τα νέα; (émathes ta néa = did you hear the news?).

target: Κατάλαβα το μάθημα με τη βοήθειά σου.
english: I understood the lesson with your help.
tip: τη βοήθειά σου (ti voítheiá sou = your help) has two accents: with σου (sou) attached, stress would sit too far from the end, so a second accent is added.

target: Βγήκαμε για ποτό με τους συναδέλφους.
english: We went out for a drink with the colleagues.
tip: βγαίνω για = go out for: βγήκαμε για ποτό (vgíkame gia potó = we went out for a drink).

target: Πήρες τηλέφωνο τη μαμά σου;
english: Did you call your mom?
tip: παίρνω τηλέφωνο = to phone someone: πήρες τηλέφωνο; (píres tiléfono = did you call?)

target: Τι κάνατε το σαββατοκύριακο;
english: What did you do at the weekend?
tip: One vowel is the whole difference: κάνετε (kánete = you do) vs κάνατε (kánate = you did). Listen for the a.

target: Όταν ήμουν μικρός, έμενα σε ένα χωριό.
english: When I was little, I lived in a village.
tip: 'Used to' is built into the verb form itself: έμενα (émena = I used to live) – no extra words needed.

target: Πηγαίναμε κάθε καλοκαίρι στο ίδιο νησί.
english: Every summer we went to the same island.
tip: Habits take the imperfect: κάθε καλοκαίρι πηγαίναμε (káthe kalokaíri pigaíname = every summer we went).
